title: GLM-5.3 vs. Claude Fable 5 on DeepSWE: Cost, Coding, and Routing
gist: On Together AI's DeepSWE benchmark, GLM-5.3 and Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 tie on first-attempt coding accuracy, but GLM-5.3 costs 5.4x less per rollout and pulls ahead on every multi-attempt metric, making it the default choice with Fable relegated to a narrow, expensive escalation for Rust and serialization work.

insights.claim: GLM-5.3 costs $3.99 per DeepSWE rollout versus $21.63 for Claude Fable 5, a 5.4x price gap, making Fable the single most expensive configuration measured on the DeepSWE board.
insights.speaker: Together AI Blog
insights.so_what: For inference buyers, a 5.4x price gap with no accuracy advantage for the pricier model is a strong signal to default to the open-weight option and reserve the premium model for narrow use cases.
insights.quote: The cost gap is 5.4x. $3.99 per rollout vs. $21.63. Per $100 spent, GLM-5.3 solves 17 tasks and Fable solves 3.

insights.claim: Measured as tasks solved per $100 spent, GLM-5.3 delivers 17 solved tasks compared to 3 for Claude Fable 5, meaning GLM-5.3 is roughly 5.7x more cost-efficient by this measure.
insights.speaker: Together AI Blog
insights.so_what: Cost-per-solve is the metric that matters for high-volume agentic coding deployments; this gap directly favors open-weight inference providers over closed frontier labs on price-sensitive workloads.
insights.locator: GLM 5.3 vs Claude Fable 5 at a glance table

insights.claim: Despite being far cheaper, GLM-5.3 is not slower in wall-clock terms: it averages 35 minutes per rollout versus Fable's 34 minutes, so the price advantage does not come with a meaningful latency penalty.
insights.speaker: Together AI Blog
insights.so_what: A cost leader that isn't also a latency laggard removes the usual objection to switching to the cheaper model, strengthening the case for GLM-5.3 as a default.
insights.quote: GLM-5.3 averages 35 minutes per rollout against Fable's 34, roughly even.

insights.claim: A cascade strategy that runs GLM-5.3 first and escalates to Claude Fable 5 only on failure solves 81.1% of DeepSWE tasks at $10.74 per task, eleven points more accurate than Fable alone while costing half of Fable's own per-task price.
insights.speaker: Together AI Blog
insights.so_what: Model-cascade routing (cheap model first, expensive model as verifier-gated escalation) is a reusable architecture pattern for AI application builders trying to minimize inference spend without sacrificing accuracy.
insights.quote: Run GLM-5.3 first and escalate to Fable only when your test suite rejects the answer: 81.1% solved at $10.74 per task.

insights.claim: On first-attempt accuracy (pass@1), Claude Fable 5 scores 69.7% versus GLM-5.3's 69.0% on DeepSWE, a 0.7 point gap that the authors say sits inside the statistical error bars for both models.
insights.speaker: Together AI Blog
insights.so_what: A statistical tie on the headline accuracy metric between an open-weight and a closed frontier model signals that price, not quality, is now the deciding factor for many coding-agent deployment decisions.
insights.quote: Fable 5 posts 69.7% pass@1 and GLM-5.3 posts 69.0%, a 0.7 point gap that sits inside the error bars on both sides.

insights.claim: GLM-5.3 overtakes Claude Fable 5 as soon as multiple attempts are allowed, leading pass@2 81.1% to 77.1% and pass@4 87.6% to 84.1%, giving it both the lower price and the higher accuracy ceiling in any retry-tolerant setting.
insights.speaker: Together AI Blog
insights.so_what: For agentic workflows that already support retries (most production coding agents do), GLM-5.3 dominates Fable on both cost and ceiling accuracy, removing the case for paying the premium.
insights.quote: GLM-5.3 owns the retries. It leads pass@2 (81.1% vs. 77.1%) and pass@4 (87.6% vs. 84.1%), so it has the higher ceiling as well as the lower price.

insights.claim: Claude Fable 5 is marginally steadier per individual attempt, with 82.0% reliability versus GLM-5.3's 78.8%, and solves more tasks perfectly on all four trials (56 vs. 48), while GLM-5.3 wins on coverage (87.6% vs. 84.1% of tasks solved at least once).
insights.speaker: Together AI Blog
insights.so_what: The tradeoff between reliability (consistency per shot) and coverage (breadth of what's solvable at all) is a distinct axis from raw pass@1 and matters for teams deciding between single-shot and best-of-k deployment patterns.

insights.claim: Both GLM-5.3 and Claude Fable 5 regress (break) previously passing tests in only 11% of their failures, far below the 20% regression rate the authors attribute to GPT-family models, indicating both are relatively safe to accept without heavy regression gating.
insights.speaker: Together AI Blog
insights.so_what: Regression rate is a proxy for how much verification infrastructure a team must build around a model's output; a shared low regression rate across GLM-5.3 and Fable versus GPT models is a competitive data point for both against OpenAI's family.
insights.quote: Both models regress the existing test suite in only 11% of failures, far below the GPT-family's 20%, so both are safe to accept without heavy regression gating.

insights.claim: When Claude Fable 5 fails, it is more often badly wrong (18% big-miss share vs. GLM-5.3's 16%), while GLM-5.3 more often fails by a near miss (61% vs. 57%), indicating the two models share a similar, disciplined failure signature.
insights.speaker: Together AI Blog
insights.so_what: Similar failure signatures across models from different labs (open-weight Zhipu-linked GLM vs. closed Anthropic-style Fable) suggest failure mode may be more a function of training philosophy/discipline than of model origin or scale.

insights.claim: GLM-5.3 wins five of eight task domains against Claude Fable 5, including a 17-point lead in concurrency and durability (62% vs. 45%, Fable's weakest domain), plus wins in query/config, language/runtime internals, stateful reactivity, and program analysis.
insights.speaker: Together AI Blog
insights.so_what: Concurrency and durability work is a common pain point for coding agents; a 17-point edge there is a concrete reason to route systems-level concurrent code specifically to GLM-5.3.
insights.quote: That concurrency result is a 17-point gap in Fable's weakest domain.
insights.locator: Where each wins, by task type

insights.claim: Claude Fable 5's strength is concentrated in exact-contract domains: data modeling and serialization (88% vs. 79%), build and ops (71% vs. 68%), and protocol conformance (55% vs. 44%, GLM-5.3's weakest area).
insights.speaker: Together AI Blog
insights.so_what: Protocol conformance and serialization are the specific domains where paying the Fable premium is justified; outside these, the premium buys little.
insights.locator: Where each wins, by task type

insights.claim: Claude Fable 5's biggest edge is Rust, where it scores 85% versus GLM-5.3's 70%, a 15-point gap that is the widest single-language margin in the entire comparison and the primary justification for using Fable at all.
insights.speaker: Together AI Blog
insights.so_what: For teams doing Rust-heavy development, Fable's premium may be worth paying selectively; for everyone else the article argues it is not.
insights.quote: Its Rust is 85% to GLM's 70, a 15-point margin and the widest single-language gap in the matchup.
insights.locator: GLM-5.3 vs. Claude Fable 5 by programming language

insights.claim: GLM-5.3 posts the best JavaScript score of any model measured (90% vs. Fable's 75%), is near parity on Go (76% vs. 71%), and edges TypeScript (61% vs. 57%), while Fable holds a smaller lead in Python (70% vs. 66%).
insights.speaker: Together AI Blog
insights.so_what: A best-in-class JavaScript score for an open-weight model is a notable competitive marker against closed frontier labs, relevant for web-development-focused coding agent products choosing a backend model.
insights.quote: GLM answers with the best JavaScript on the board (90 vs 75)
insights.locator: GLM-5.3 vs. Claude Fable 5 by programming language

insights.claim: GLM-5.3 and Claude Fable 5 have a per-task correlation of 0.65, the highest agreement of any model pairing measured by the authors, meaning the two models tend to succeed and fail on the same tasks and thus add little diversity value when run together.
insights.speaker: Together AI Blog
insights.so_what: High correlation between models is a signal against building expensive multi-model ensembles for that pairing; portfolio/ensemble value only shows up with lower-correlation pairs (e.g., a GPT-family model).
insights.quote: Per-task correlation between GLM-5.3 and Fable is 0.65, the highest agreement of any pairing in this set.
insights.locator: How similar are GLM-5.3 and Claude Fable 5?

insights.claim: The article's core investment thesis is that when two models are near-substitutes on quality, the price gap becomes the entire decision, and the practical recommendation is GLM-5.3 as the default model with Claude Fable 5 reserved only for Rust-heavy or serialization-critical escalation.
insights.speaker: Together AI Blog
insights.so_what: This is a direct positioning argument for Together AI's own inference offering (serving GLM-5.3) against Anthropic's proprietary model on cost grounds, a competitive narrative relevant to the inference-market landscape.
insights.quote: When two models are this close on quality, the price gap becomes the entire decision.

insights.claim: Together AI positions GLM-5.3 as open-weight (self-hostable or servable through inference providers such as Together AI) while Claude Fable 5 is closed and available only through Anthropic and its partners.
insights.speaker: Together AI Blog
insights.so_what: Open-weight availability is a structural distribution advantage for Together AI's business model, letting it capture inference revenue on a model that performs at near-parity with closed frontier alternatives.
insights.quote: GLM-5.3 is an open-weight model, so it can be self-hosted or served through inference providers such as Together AI. Claude Fable 5 is a closed model available only through Anthropic and its partners.

insights.claim: The comparison used 113 DeepSWE v1.1 tasks with 4 trials per model at max effort settings (904 total rollouts, 452 per model), scored using DeepSWE's official scoring which excludes infrastructure errors; Fable had 16 infra errors versus GLM-5.3's 1, so Fable's strict errors-as-failures score (67.3%) is notably lower than its official score (69.7%).
insights.speaker: Together AI Blog
insights.so_what: Fable's higher infra-error count under identical test conditions is itself a data point on routing/infrastructure reliability that investors evaluating Anthropic's serving stack for this model should note.
insights.quote: Fable has 16 infra errors from model routing, so its strict errors-as-failures score is 67.3 against 69.7 official. GLM-5.3 has 1.
